name: The young shore cottonwoods at Sixteenth to Eighteenth Street

existence.note: INFERRED, AS THE 1835 GROVE IS. Moses and Kirkland (1895, p. 60) put 'scattered cottonwoods, and here and there a small group or a single tree' on the lower reaches of this shore in 1812, and the same page has Mrs. Kinzie's word that the two massacre trees were saplings then. Clarke's grove of 1835 (Kirkland 1893, App. K) stood on ground no source clears or plants in the years between, so its trees were growing here in 1812. Which of them were already standing, and how tall, nobody records.
